title: Rayon row-tile multithread for B1/B3 dense kernels
description:
Apply rayon row-tile parallelism to the post-Tier-B dense kernels (transpose, M4RM tile-reuse multiply). Pre-flight cache-miss check is mandatory — multithreading a memory-bound kernel adds bus contention without throughput.

## Background

`crates/gf2-core/src/compute/cpu.rs` already has rayon-parallel M4RM/RREF/rank, but the kernels delivered by Tier B (transpose, M4RM tile-reuse multiply) need their parallel scheduling tuned to the new tile shapes.

Pre-flight (mandatory before V10): run `perf stat -r 10` on the post-Tier-B single-thread kernel. If `cache-misses / instructions $> 1\%$` the kernel is memory-bound and multithreading will hurt — abort and revert.

If pre-flight passes, V10 applies rayon row-tile parallelism over the post-Tier-B tile shape using `rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder` with the project's existing thread-count convention. Tile boundaries align to 64-byte cache lines to avoid false sharing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Pre-flight `perf stat` cache-miss check executed and recorded in the JIT issue.
- [hard] No correctness regression vs. single-threaded path (existing tests pass under multi-thread).
- [hard] Strong-scaling efficiency $\geq 70\%$ at 4 threads at the design size class.
- [hard] False-sharing check: tile boundaries align to 64-byte cache lines.
- [hard] Strong-scaling measured at 1, 2, 4, 8 threads; numbers recorded.
- [aspirational] $\geq 3\times$ total speedup over the post-Tier-B single-thread baseline at 4 threads.

## Notes

Bench: post-Tier-B variants of `matmul` and the new `transpose` bench. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
